cells.remarks: In three portions. The first portion, in the front of the footprint records the death of Muto Bāsha(kha) tamalaji, the son of Muto Chunnamaji mahājana (i.e. a merchant) on the first date and the installation of the footprints of the person. The second portion, to the right of the footprint, records the renovation probably of the chhatrī, on the third date by Lālā-bhaṭṭa. The various renovations of the portions, some of which belonged to Gwalior. The third portion, to the left of the footprints, records that the chhatrī was constructed on the bank of the field belonging to the gaṁhiṁa Gussanī Rājyāṁha and Rīpachandra. By Rīpachandra, Dāṁs-ida chhaṁde when Osaṁhī Rājyāṁha was the pontiff. The masons were Bālākisana and Gaṁgārāma. For the first portion Cf. ibid., No. 512.

Further states that between the second and third dates, in the reign of the Queen, by the advice of Mr. G. N. Nox, Mr. E.F. Moon and Mr. M.P. D’Cruz, Deputy Commissioner, the tank was closed and repaired, the debris cleared, and fruit trees planted for beautifying the place. It also states that the cleaning and repair work was done by the contribution and donation received by the Municipal Committee. Lastly, it gives a list of donors and the amount of donation in each case.
